paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: Illustrating the empirical generalization errors and sharpness measures with respect to QLoRA weights. (<ref>) Smaller adapters with a rank of 16 achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima. (<ref>) An ensemble of k adapters leads to lower generalization errors and Hessian traces. Here, we fix the sum of the dimensions of k adapters to be equal to 256. (<ref>) QLoRA, which is trained on a quantized base model, yields lower generalization errors and Hessian trace values compared to LoRA.

model_annotations.Bulgarian: The figure illustrates the relationship between model rank and error (RTE), showing how generalization error changes with different adapter ranks in the context of QLoRA fine-tuning. The horizontal axis, labeled "Rank," is a logarithmic scale with values at 4, 16, 64, and 256, representing the rank of the low-rank adapters. The vertical axis, labeled "Error (RTE)," is a linear scale ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, with major gridlines at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9. A single line plot is shown, connecting four data points, each represented by a green circle with vertical error bars indicating variability. The line begins at a rank of 4 with an error of approximately 0.55, decreases to a minimum error of about 0.5 at a rank of 16, then increases to around 0.55 at a rank of 64, and finally rises to approximately 0.63 at a rank of 256. The error bars are present at all four points, with the largest bars observed at the highest rank (256).
model_annotations.English: The line plot illustrates the relationship between error (measured as RTE, or Repeated Training Error) and the rank of adapters used in fine-tuning language models, with data points corresponding to ranks of 4, 16, 64, and 256. The x-axis, labeled "Rank," is a linear scale with tick marks at these four values, representing the dimensionality of the adapter matrices. The y-axis, labeled "Error (RTE)," is also linear, ranging from 0.3 to 0.9, and quantifies the generalization error. Each data point is represented by a green circle with error bars indicating variability, and the points are connected by a solid black line. The error starts at approximately 0.55 for rank 4, decreases to a minimum of about 0.48 at rank 16, then increases to around 0.53 at rank 64, and rises further to approximately 0.63 at rank 256. This trend visually supports the caption's claim that smaller adapters (rank 16) achieve the lowest generalization errors, with performance degrading as the rank increases. The presence of error bars suggests statistical uncertainty in the measured errors, particularly at the higher ranks.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm zeigt die generalisierungsfähigen Fehler (Error, RTE) in Abhängigkeit vom Rang (Rank) für verschiedene Adapterkonfigurationen, wobei die Fehlerwerte als durchgehende Linie mit grünen Kreis-Markierungen dargestellt sind und Fehlerbalken die Unsicherheit der Messungen anzeigen. Die x-Achse repräsentiert den Rang mit den Werten 4, 16, 64 und 256, wobei die Beschriftungen in einem logarithmischen Skalierungsverlauf angeordnet sind und die Achse als numerische, nichtlineare Skala mit festen Tick-Markierungen dargestellt ist. Die y-Achse zeigt den Fehler (RTE) in einem linearen Skalierungsverlauf mit Werten von 0.3 bis 0.9, wobei die Beschriftungen in Schritten von 0.3 angegeben sind. Die Linie beginnt bei einem Rang von 4 mit einem Fehlerwert von etwa 0.58, fällt dann bei einem Rang von 16 auf etwa 0.53, steigt bei einem Rang von 64 auf etwa 0.56 und erreicht schließlich bei einem Rang von 256 einen Wert von etwa 0.65. Die Fehlerbalken zeigen eine relativ geringe Varianz bei den Werten 4, 16 und 64, während sie bei Rang 256 größer wird, was auf eine höhere Unsicherheit bei diesem Wert hindeutet.
